posts.title: Bedraggled: A Rain-Soaked White Trillium
posts.description: In early May, after a violent storm, I visit my beloved Shindagin Hollow and come across a rain-beaten Great White Trillium (Trillium grandiflorum), growing on the bank of a forest brook. The scene is lovely, with fern fronds unfolding to one side and the gurgling brook in the background. It is still raining lightly and a Veery thrush is calling and singing nearby. posts.title: Red Squirrels Harvesting Spruce Cones
posts.description: One early autumn day, I visit a Norway Spruce stand and quickly discover the trees are alive with Red Squirrel activity. The squirrels are busy cutting cones from limbs high in the canopy and then dropping them to the ground. posts.title: Thunder-Pumper
posts.description: It is dawn in a vast prairie wetland in central North Dakota. I sit quietly in my canoe, alongside a dense stand of cattails and rushes. The marsh is alive with bird sounds, but I am here specifically to record the resonant, gulping onk-ka-chonk (or pumper-lunk ) of an American Bittern, hidden in thick vegetation less than a hundred feet away.
